card_says: The company name on the card gives the shareholdings as Eskom 44% and Globeleq 56% at the start, with a 20-year distribution concession from 2005.
source_says: Those were the holdings at the start. By the end of the concession Umeme was listed on the Uganda Securities Exchange and cross-listed on the Nairobi Securities Exchange, and the 2025 report mentions neither Eskom nor Globeleq. The 20-year concession ended on 31 March 2025, when the network was handed to the state company UEDCL; headcount then fell from 2,409 to 18 and the company says it no longer has operating activities.

source.title: After 20 years in Uganda, Umeme is now eyeing Sierra Leone

card_says: Coal miner obliged to resettle, headquarters Rio de Janeiro, Brazil.
source_says: Vale bought the Colombian coal assets in 2008 for US$308 million and by June 2012 had agreed to sell 100% of the El Hatillo mine, the Cerro Largo deposit, Sociedad Portuaria Rio Cordoba and an 8.43% stake in the FENOCO railway to Goldman Sachs-controlled Colombia Natural Resources, subject to Colombian government approval. Murray Energy then bought Colombia Natural Resources from Goldman Sachs on 14 August 2015, taking the La Francia and El Hatillo surface mines, three undeveloped mines, an Atlantic coal port and an 8.4% stake in the Fenoco railroad, with estimated reserves of 184 million tons, and renamed the Colombian mines Murray Colombian Resources. A Rio de Janeiro head office fits the Vale period up to 2012 rather than the owners that followed.

source.title: Goldman-controlled Colombian Natural Resources to buy Vale's mines

The card's wording may describe the position at the time of the case rather than now.
